title: Не смотри ему в глаза  (Do Not Look into His Eyes)

segments.t: Approaching the moustached man's table with eyes averted, Max invents one excuse after another—from a problem with his room to a parked car outside—to make him leave the dining room. When Max accidentally looks into his eyes and feels nothing, he tackles the man.
Простите, пожалуйста, вас там к ресепшену вызывают.
Ошиблись, я не живу в этом отеле.
А вас вроде в гардероб позовут.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Do not look into his eyes!' Kostya anchors the line on 'not', while 'eyes' completes the thought. Max answers right away.
Простите, пожалуйста, вас там к ресепшену вызывают.
'Excuse me, please, they are calling you to reception over there.' Max brings out the contrast between 'forgive' and 'please' in a few short words.
Ошиблись, я не живу в этом отеле.
'They made a mistake, I do not live in this hotel.' The grammar packs 'made a mistake' and 'hotel' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'You know, I mixed it up.' The grammar packs 'you' and 'mixed up' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'They are asking you to repark your car.' Max anchors the line on 'you', while 'car' completes the thought.
'I am without a car.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'cars' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
А вас вроде в гардероб позовут.
'And it seems they are calling you to the cloakroom.' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'will call' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. the inspector answers right away.
'What is going on?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'what' before landing on 'is happening'.
'I looked into his eyes!' Max anchors the line on 'I', while 'looked at' completes the thought.
'And do you know who I am?' The grammar packs 'and' and 'I' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Max answers right away.
'A fraudster! You did not pay the bill!' Notice how Russian expresses 'con artist' and 'score' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Everything is fine!' In Russian, the idea of 'everything' flows naturally into 'normally' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Простите, пожалуйста, вас там к ресепшену вызывают.
Ошиблись, я не живу в этом отеле.
А вас вроде в гардероб позовут.
And that concludes the dining room ambush. Notice how every excuse fails until Max looks straight at the guest and mistakenly arrests him. See you in the next scene.
